title: Sparing, consistent emphasis
statement: Use emphasis sparingly and consistently, with no all-caps, because emphasis on one fragment can tell learners that only that fragment needs an answer.
detail: Review feedback of 11 August 2026 on a Grade 5 reference lesson asked for consistent type styling in a modelled response, so that emphasis does not imply learners answer only one fragment, and asked that hints avoid all-caps emphasis and use bold only when sparing emphasis is necessary. The course's instruction-review profile maps both to a criterion that rejects learner-facing language that is over-emphasized, among other faults. The mapping implies no verdict on the current course.

evidence.quote: Use consistent type styling so emphasis does not imply that learners answer only one fragment.
Avoid all-caps emphasis and use bold only when sparing emphasis is necessary.
Language is inaccurate, developmentally mismatched, inconsistently named, over-emphasized, or incorrectly punctuated.
Map every distinct August 11 reviewer observation to the reusable instruction-review criteria without claiming that the current Grade 5 delivery has passed.
